text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday: NEUE ZUERCHER ZEITUNG - Finance Minister Kaspar Villiger told the Radical Democrats' party convention in Zug last Saturday the party will not gain any voters due to internal divisions. The delegates also turned down a proposal for public referendum on introducing a repressive durg policy in Switzerland. - Manpower Job index in Juli rose by 1.3 percentage points to 38.2 percent. The index is based on the number of job ads in newspapers. TAGES ANZEIGER - The Swiss stock exchange lost more than six percent last week. Hanspeter Lutz, director with the Bank Vontobel, told journalists in an interview that small investors should hold out. - Credit Suisse chairman Rainer Gut said he may get out of conventional banking business in the U.S. or sell the U.S. activities of Winterthur as part of the approval process in connection with the planned merger. JOURNAL DE GENEVE - Andreas Durisch was appointed new editor-in-chief at Sunday newspaper SonntagsZeitung, replacing Ueli Haldimann, who was fired after the paper published a wrong quote by Swiss politician Christopf Blocher.
